- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at +2% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (avg > 0.3) and model is flat or declining, force a slight upward bias (e.g., +0.3–0.8% per day) to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term trend (30d) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to 30d horizon if sentiment > 0.1 over last 7 days.
- If model forecast is below 70.0 and sentiment is positive, avoid downward correction — instead, assume momentum will carry price above 70.5; set floor at 70.5 unless sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive (e.g., >+0.5 in 3 days), model often lags; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast 3–5 days ahead to capture sentiment shift.
- If model forecast is >75.0 and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection from recent spikes.
- Model tends to overfit short-term volatility; for 30d forecasts, smooth out sharp peaks and troughs by applying a 0.5–1.0% dampening factor if sentiment is volatile (std > 0.3).
